clue.text: Joke too blue, perhaps

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease or joke with them
too in the sense of 'as well' can be rendered as and

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a joke is far too smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a comment on the joke's crudeness, but a blue is a ribbon awarded as a prize, hence a riband.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue (as in the Blue Riband prize) is one example of a ribbon awarded for distinction.

clue.text: Revered figure in holding company

indicators.note: the word in holds the company abbreviation inside it

explanation.surface: A respected figurehead is employed by a holding company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding company' looks like a single business phrase, but the two words do separate jobs: 'holding' is the container signal and 'company' gives its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol, someone worshipped or venerated, is a revered figure.

clue.text: Profit that one shouldn't take unfairly

definitions.text: Profit that one shouldn't take unfairly

parts.words: Profit that one shouldn't take unfairly
parts.note: a gain or benefit which, in the idiom, one should not take of others

explanation.definitionFit: A benefit or gain; taking it of someone means exploiting them unfairly.

clue.text: Gather I have to support a revolutionary uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second part sits under the first and holds it up
in a down clue, uprising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone backs a revolutionary rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns RED into DER; 'to support' puts IVE below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in the sense of conclude or infer: you derive a meaning from evidence.

clue.text: Not liable to be stumped for a pay demand

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batter standing inside the crease (the line in front of the stumps) cannot be stumped out
a call for a rise in wages

explanation.surface: A cricketer safe from dismissal sends in a request for more money.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN CREASE: a cricket batter with bat or foot behind the crease line cannot be stumped by the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage demand asks for a rise, and a rise in pay is called a raise or boost by synonym.

clue.text: One nurse can ruin schedule, maybe for life

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: ruin breaks up the letters of nurse can

parts.note: a policy is a plan or schedule of action

explanation.surface: A single nurse could wreck the timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Life cover is one type of such a contract, so the 'maybe' signals an example.

clue.text: Bob identifies two causes of power failure

parts.note: a cut in the supply stops the power
a short circuit trips the electricity

explanation.surface: A man called Bob works out why the lights went out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the verb, as in bobbing hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob hair is to trim it, so the verb means curtail or abbreviate.

clue.text: Ninety, in general, to rise and shine

indicators.note: ninety goes inside the general
in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A soldier is told it is time to rise and shine.
explanation.walkthrough: The general is Robert E. Lee of the American Civil War; in a down clue 'to rise' means reading upward, which gives a fish, and 'in' puts the Roman ninety inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine at something is to be outstanding, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Jammed cylinders

parts.note: jammed suggests stuck engine parts, but it means filled with jam, rolled into a tube

explanation.definitionFit: These sponge cakes are spread with jam and rolled into a cylindrical shape.

clue.text: Makes believe they have new faith

definitions.meaning: brings someone round to a belief, a verb
people who have adopted a new religion, a plural noun

explanation.surface: People pretend they have found religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes believe' reads as the idiom for pretending, but here it means causes someone to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone over to a creed is a verb sense; people won over to a new religion is the noun sense.

clue.text: Pretend to be in spasm in ruse

indicators.note: the pretending is placed inside the spasm word

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or spasm
to act is to pretend

explanation.surface: Someone fakes a fit as a trick to get out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a stratagem, a planned manoeuvre to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Yet three sevens turn out to be around fifty

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the fifty
the letters of three sevens turn out differently, rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A gambler's three sevens come to about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges THREE SEVENS into NEVERTHEESS, and 'around' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet as a conjunction means however or all the same, a concessive sense.

clue.text: Chap to turn up after one, not on time for work

indicators.note: the turned word follows the one

parts.note: a chap is a man
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turn reverses the following word up

parts.note: taken as written
late means not on time

explanation.surface: A man arrives late for work after turning up at one.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something, like dough or clay, is to handle and shape it.

clue.text: So long, and thanks, thanks again

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
ta again, the second time the thanks is given

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye and thank you twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you; TA-TA is a British informal goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal farewells, the British nursery word for goodbye.

clue.text: He has a telling part in play

definitions.text: He has a telling part in play

parts.words: He has a telling part in play
parts.note: a telling part sounds like a decisive role, but it is literally the part of one who tells the story on stage

explanation.definitionFit: The person in a drama who recounts the story to the audience is its storyteller.

clue.text: Can anyone disguise such irritation?

indicators.note: to disguise the letters of can anyone is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is possible to hide one's exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation or exasperation is a synonym of irritation.

clue.text: Took notice, got drunk, enlisted

indicators.note: getting drunk muddles the letters of enlisted

explanation.surface: A recruit paid attention, got drunk, then signed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid attention by hearing, heeded, a synonym for took notice.

clue.text: If retired, live somewhere warm

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word if is turned backwards

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: A pensioner plans to move to a warmer climate after retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If retired' suggests a pensioner, but 'retired' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth area in front of a lit fire is a cosy, heated spot in a house.

clue.text: New line that starts from Victoria

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of line

explanation.surface: A new railway line runs out of London's Victoria station.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria suggests the London station and its trains; in fact it is Lake Victoria, the main source of the great African river.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Nile flows out of Lake Victoria in Uganda, the river's traditional source.

clue.text: Collector's opening bid for chest

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an offer is a bid at auction

explanation.surface: A collector makes a first bid for an antique chest at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox for valuables, a synonym of chest.

clue.text: Discount only? Free? Here, everything comes off!

indicators.note: free means loosened, letting the letters of discount only be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop advertises discounts, or even giveaways, where everything comes off the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything comes off' sounds like a sale; in fact it is clothing coming off.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist community is a place where residents go without clothes, so all garments are removed.

clue.text: Bill is a first name

parts.note: taken as written
ac is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Bill is someone's Christian name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the name; it is a bill, AC for account.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch's name is used as a given name.

clue.text: Berliner's odd bits of cheese

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of Berliner are taken

explanation.surface: A German speaks of some strange pieces of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese with an edible white rind, an example of cheese.

clue.text: Is able to accept two articles for the Promised Land

indicators.note: the able word takes on the articles that follow it

parts.note: can means is able
a is the indefinite article
an is the other form of the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone capable takes in two items on the way to the Promised Land.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible God promised this territory to Abraham and his descendants.

clue.text: Home supporter shot in foot

parts.note: in means at home
a fan supports a team
a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A home fan's shot ends up in their foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like part of the body; it means foot soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers are troops who fight on foot, so foot is a collective term for them.

clue.text: Club porter after a drink may resort to this

definitions.text: Club porter after a drink may resort to this

indicators.note: the porter comes after the drink in the answer

parts.note: tea is a drink
a caddy carries a golfer's clubs

explanation.surface: A golf bag-carrier wanting a cuppa might reach for this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club porter' suggests a doorman at a gentlemen's club; it is a golf caddy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin or box for storing tea leaves is where someone wanting a brew would turn.

clue.text: How one danced when not quite sober?

definitions.meaning: danced a reel, a lively Scottish dance

explanation.definitionFit: Lurched unsteadily or danced a Scottish reel, both senses of the same verb.
